method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **This page covers gynaecological causes only** — other causes of acute abdominal pain must also be considered.
claims.source_text: This guideline focuses on gynaecological causes of abdominal and pelvic pain. Other causes for acute abdominal pain must also be considered
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Obstetric emergencies** (ectopic pregnancy, miscarriage, placental abruption, uterine rupture) **and gynaecological emergencies** (ovarian or adnexal torsion) **need urgent gynaecological or surgical referral.**
claims.source_text: Obstetric emergencies (eg ectopic pregnancy, miscarriage, placental abruption and uterine rupture) and gynaecological emergencies (eg ovarian or adnexal torsion) require urgent gynaecological or surgical referral
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Torsion is a clinical diagnosis; do not delay gynaecological referral for investigations such as ultrasound.**
claims.source_text: Ovarian or adnexal torsion are clinical diagnoses, and gynaecological referral should not be delayed by investigations (eg ultrasound)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Menstrual history:** menarche, LMP, cycle frequency, duration, flow, pain, flooding, **clots larger than 2 cm**, pad/tampon change frequency.
claims.source_text: Menstrual history: menarche, last menstrual period, frequency, duration, flow, pain, flooding, large clots (>2 cm in diameter), frequency of pad/tampon changes
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Also ask** about vaginal discharge, pain characteristics (sudden onset, quality, severity, triggers, bowel/bladder symptoms, fever, vomiting), sexual history and contraception, systemic features, and a HEADSS screen.
claims.source_text: Vaginal discharge Pain characteristics: location, time course eg sudden onset, quality, severity, triggers and associated symptoms eg bowel, bladder, fever, nausea, vomiting Sexual history and contraception. If sexually active discuss safe sex and contraception Systemic features: fever, weight loss, vomiting, headache Adolescent assessment (HEADSS screen)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Non-specific episodic pain:** consider constipation, abdominal migraine and functional abdominal pain.
claims.source_text: For non-specific, episodic abdominal pain, consider chronic conditions such as constipation, abdominal migraine and functional abdominal pain
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Examine for pallor, hypotension, tachycardia and an abdominal (uterine or ovarian) mass.** **Vaginal examination is rarely indicated** — discuss with a senior clinician and perform it only once.
claims.source_text: Pallor, hypotension, tachycardia Abdominal mass (uterine or ovarian) Vaginal examination is rarely indicated. It should be discussed with a senior clinician, and if needed should only be performed once
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Ovarian or adnexal torsion:** acute, sudden, sharp pelvic pain, unilateral (usually right lower quadrant) or generalised, may be intermittent; adnexal mass; nausea and vomiting.
claims.source_text: Ovarian or adnexal torsion Pelvic pain: acute/sudden onset, sharp, unilateral (usually right lower quadrant) or generalised, may be intermittent Adnexal mass Nausea and vomiting
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Ectopic pregnancy:** abdominal/pelvic pain, missed period then vaginal bleeding, possible shoulder-tip pain.
claims.source_text: Ectopic pregnancy Abdominal/pelvic pain Missed period with subsequent vaginal bleeding Can have shoulder tip pain
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Acute placental abruption:** vaginal bleeding, abdominal and/or back pain, contractions and DIC in severe cases; any gestation, peak 24–26 weeks.
claims.source_text: Acute placental abruption Vaginal bleeding Abdominal and/or back pain Uterine contractions in severe cases Disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) Any gestation (peak between 24–26 weeks)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Uterine rupture:** uterine tenderness, peritonism, vaginal bleeding, abnormal fetal heart rate. **Molar pregnancy:** vaginal bleeding, pelvic pain, enlarged uterus, severe vomiting.
claims.source_text: Uterine rupture Uterine tenderness Peritoneal irritation Vaginal bleeding Abnormal fetal heart rate Molar pregnancy Vaginal bleeding Pelvic pain Enlarged uterus Severe vomiting
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **PID:** risk factors such as unprotected sex, post-coital bleeding, mucopurulent discharge, lower abdominal or pelvic pain, fever.
claims.source_text: Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) Risk factors (eg unprotected sex) Post coital bleeding Mucopurulent discharge Lower abdominal or pelvic pain Fever
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Mittelschmerz:** mild unilateral recurrent midcycle pain. **Ruptured ovarian cyst:** sudden, severe unilateral pelvic pain, can follow strenuous activity.
claims.source_text: Mittelschmerz Mild unilateral recurrent midcycle pain caused by normal follicular enlargement Ruptured ovarian cyst Sudden, severe, unilateral pelvic pain, can be precipitated by strenuous physical activity
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Endometriosis:** crampy pelvic pain with menses, possibly with pain on defecation, urination or intercourse.
claims.source_text: Endometriosis Crampy pelvic pain associated with menses. Depending on its location can be associated with pain on passing stool or urine, or during sexual intercourse
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Imperforate hymen:** amenorrhoea, cyclical pain, vaginal distension causing back pain or pain on defecation or urination. **Retained foreign body:** discharge, intermittent bleeding or spotting.
claims.source_text: Imperforate hymen Amenorrhoea Cyclical pain Marked distension of the vagina may cause back pain or pain with defaecation or urination Retained foreign body Vaginal discharge Intermittent bleeding or spotting
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do a βhCG (with consent)** — urine, and/or blood if a quantitative result is needed.
claims.source_text: Perform (with consent) a ßhCG (urine and/or blood if need a quantitative result)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Critical cause suspected: pelvic ultrasound**, transabdominal (full bladder) or transvaginal (sexually active, with consent) — but never delaying torsion referral.
claims.source_text: If features to suggest a critical cause Ovarian/adnexal torsion is a clinical diagnosis and requires urgent gynaecological referral that should not be delayed by investigations eg ultrasound Pelvic ultrasound: transabdominal (with full bladder) or transvaginal (in sexually active adolescents with consent)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Infection suspected:** urine MCS; first-pass urine NAAT for *Chlamydia trachomatis* and *Neisseria gonorrhoeae*, or a vaginal/endocervical swab for gonorrhoea, chlamydia and MCS; FBE, CRP ± blood culture if PID or sepsis is a real concern.
claims.source_text: If features of infection Urine MCS to exclude UTI First pass urine (nucleic acid amplification tests) for Chlamydia trachomatis, Neisseria gonorrhoeae and … self-collected vaginal swab or clinician-collected endocervical swab for gonorrhoea, chlamydia and MCS FBE, CRP +/- blood culture if high degree of concern for pelvic inflammatory disease or sepsis
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consult the local paediatric team** for haemodynamic instability, marked pain or unclear cause.
claims.source_text: Consider consultation with local paediatric team when Child with haemodynamic instability, marked pain or unclear cause
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Urgent gynaecology (or surgical) consultation** for suspected torsion, ectopic pregnancy, threatened miscarriage or non-viable pregnancy; also for causes needing surgery, and PID.
claims.source_text: Consultation with gynaecological (or surgical) team when Suspected ovarian or adnexal torsion or ectopic pregnancy/threatened miscarriage/non-viable pregnancy (urgent) Causes requiring surgical intervention Pelvic inflammatory disease
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when stable with a GP review scheduled.**
claims.source_text: Consider discharge when Stable and a review is scheduled with a GP
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Adolescent gynaecology - lower abdominal pain' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Adolescent_Gynaecology_Lower_Abdominal_Pain/, retrieved 2026-09-23
